subject_repointed.reasoning: After l-006 the run does write the resolved container's details back onto the ALERTED vertex v-001 — class becomes dev-tools/internal/known-corp, and container_name=db-1, image, service are attached to it. That is some marking of what was resolved, so this is not a bare 'no'. But the identity cell itself is never restated: v-001's ident remains `soc-playground`, and the run simultaneously writes attrs.kind=vm onto that same vertex, which asserts the outer host rather than the container. I looked for a later `:R attr_updates` row with key `ident` on v-001, and for any sentence in the record naming which entity the disposition is about; neither exists. The closing summary keeps both entities in play in one sentence ('the sudo burst on soc-playground ... Container e5b0213bd690 (db-1) runs PostgreSQL 14') without ever saying which one is the subject. Container facts folded onto a vertex still identified as the host is a merge, not a re-point.

governance_reasked.reasoning: Every query against the four governance systems in the QUERY TABLE runs before the resolving lead l-006, and every one names the alerted host: cmdb.host-trust-edges params={"host": "soc-playground"}, cmdb.list-all-hosts params={}, change-mgmt.active-changes params={"at": "2026-08-30T09:54:00Z", "host": "soc-playground"}, change-mgmt.list-changes params={"host": "soc-playground"}, ticket.search-soc-playground params={"q": "soc-playground"}, ticket.open-incidents and ticket.all-tickets. The identity system is never queried at all, at any point. The only queries after l-006 are the five l-005 elastic history queries, all of which still filter on host.name == "soc-playground" and none of which touch cmdb, identity, change-mgmt, or ticket. I searched the table for any post-l-006 call to those four systems carrying a parameter naming db-1, e5b0213bd690, or soc-playground/host-db:22.04 — there is none. The host-state calls at l-006 resolve the container but are not governance systems.

evidence: The host is unmanaged in CMDB and has no change ticket, but the activity is authorized by container design: a database server running postgres initialization during startup is expected behavior.
l-003|e-001|ac1|unauthorized|change-mgmt|"zero change tickets exist for soc-playground in the change-management system"
The authz contract ac1 (on h-001, now `--`) was resolved as unauthorized — no change window exists. Since h-001 is non-surviving, this does not block disposition.
closing_claim_scoped.reasoning: The conclude block has no `ceiling_test` field at all, so the ceiling claim lives in the disposition rationale — and there it is scoped to the alerted host, not to the entity the run investigated. 'The host is unmanaged in CMDB and has no change ticket' rests entirely on the loop-1 lookups keyed to soc-playground, all of which predate the container resolution. The run then discharges that adverse governance finding not by re-checking db-1 but by asserting 'the activity is authorized by container design' — an appeal to what the container is, using no governance record for the container, which was never requested. The one authz contract that was resolved (ac1, unauthorized) is set aside on the grounds that its parent hypothesis did not survive, so no governance question ends up answered about db-1. The claim asserts absence from systems that were only ever asked about a different entity.

summary: The run resolved the container at l-006 and then folded its details — name db-1, image, PostgreSQL 14 service — onto the alerted host vertex while leaving that vertex's identity reading `soc-playground` and even writing kind=vm onto it. That is a merge of two entities into one row, not a turn-around. No governance system was consulted again afterwards: the only post-resolution work is five Falco history queries still filtered on host.name == "soc-playground", and identity was never queried at any point in the run. The close then makes its governance claim about the wrong entity — 'the host is unmanaged in CMDB and has no change ticket' — carried over unchanged from loop 1, and neutralizes it with an appeal to 'authorized by container design' rather than any record for the container it had just identified. The bookkeeping around the container is competent; the investigation's subject never moved.
